the-import-panel-reads-the-shape-the-api.why: THE LIVE DEFECT THIS BATCH FIXED, RESTORED BYTE FOR BYTE — AND IT NO LONGER COMPILES, WHICH IS A BETTER OUTCOME THAN A FAILING TEST AND IS MEASURED RATHER THAN HOPED FOR. Phase 2 item 1 replaced the api's `rejections` and `failures` with one `issues` list, and this line kept reading both: both were `undefined`, `.length` threw, and the panel reporting on a SUCCESSFUL import died during render while the rows went into the book. It survived three weeks and every gate, because TypeScript cannot check an interface a screen declares by hand over HTTP and the Playwright fixture supplied the old fields itself. **CORRECTED FROM THE MEASUREMENT: this `why` first said `customer-import.spec.ts` fails. IT NEVER GETS THAT FAR — `npx turbo run build --filter=web` fails first** with `page.tsx(307,19): error TS2339: Property 'rejections' does not exist on type 'ImportResult'` and the same for `failures`, so Playwright cannot start at all (`Process from config.webServer was not able to start`). THE REASON IS THE REAL FIX: correcting the hand-copied interface made the old read UNREPRESENTABLE, where before it was merely wrong. That is the form this repository prefers — the shape that cannot express the mistake over the shape that requires you to notice it — and it is why the sibling plant (`the-hand-copied-shape-drifts-again`) matters more: it attacks the DECLARATION, which is the only place this class can still go wrong, and nothing in either app can see that.

the-hand-copied-shape-drifts-again.why: THE DRIFT ITSELF, ONE LAYER BEFORE THE CRASH. A field added to the WEB's declaration and not the api's is the direction that broke the screen: it is `undefined` at runtime, no type sees it, and the screen reads it. Nothing in `apps/web` or `apps/api` can catch this — two packages, two builds, and `turbo prune web --docker` means a spec in either one cannot import the other. `packages/db/prisma/legacy-import-shape-parity.spec.ts` fails on `the RESULT carries exactly the same fields on both sides`, naming `failures` in the diff, AND on `neither side still declares the fields that caused the crash` — two assertions, because the second is an ABSENCE and is the only form that catches both sides regaining the field at once, which is how they got there in the first place. THE PLANT IS DELIBERATELY `failures` RATHER THAN A NEW NAME: a plant should be the regression somebody would really write, and the realistic one here is somebody restoring what the screen used to read.

a-past-import-shows-its-counts-and-never.why: THE SECOND OF THE TWO ROUTES, UNWIRED AGAIN. `GET /imports/customers/batches/:id` is the one that carries the LINES — which line was refused and why — and the list route carries only counts. So with this plant the register still renders, every count is right, each past import still expands, and the thing the durable report exists for (*an officer who imported 2,000 rows read its refusals once*) is gone: the expander shows the all-clear sentence instead. Nothing errors. **AND THE ROUTE COUNT WOULD NOT CATCH IT EITHER** — `unreachable-routes.py` matches on the PATH, and `/imports/customers/batches` is still addressed by the list call, so the by-path pass reads this collection as reachable and the budget stays at 14. The by-VERB pass is no help: both are `GET`. `customer-import.spec.ts` fails on the test that clicks a past import and expects its DUPLICATE line — which is why that test clicks rather than only reading the list, and why the `why` says so.
